key_insight: Curved channel geometry and spatially varying shear can localise bacterial adhesion, shifting attachment toward wall peaks at lower shear and wall valleys at higher shear.
engineering_relevance: The result helps predict and control biofilm risk in industrial and medical flow systems by linking surface shape and flow conditions to where bacteria are most likely to stick.
method: Asymptotic analysis of the high-velocity diffusive boundary layer
Curvilinear coordinate system based on the fluid streamfunction
Similarity solution for a diffusivity-varying diffusion-type equation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an analytical adhesion-rate expression derived from the model and its comparison is based on predicted spatial localisation patterns rather than experimental data.
watch_item: The approach is analytical and asymptotic, so accuracy may be limited outside the high-velocity, dilute-suspension regime or for more complex wall properties.
paper_title: Bacterial adhesion to curved surfaces in fluid flow
